22.description: The committee received a summary of heritage grant funding and discussed the lack of protection for 113 identified heritage properties, which rely on owner initiative for designation.

chips.text: Recommended
Businesses in Business Improvement Districts could benefit from reinvested parking revenue.
Cost to restore and operate the Civic Conservatory remains unknown.
Administration will provide annual heritage grant funding updates for January meetings.

19.description: The Municipal Heritage Advisory Committee is reviewing heritage policies, evaluating the Heritage Awards Program, and researching intangible heritage definitions for future city policy.

chips.text: The committee's $17,000 budget is insufficient for a Heritage Awards dinner event.
Property owners who invest in heritage preservation are recognized through awards.
Why was intangible heritage previously removed from the city's heritage policy?
The committee will explore partnerships for the Heritage Awards Program.

18.description: The committee discussed defining "intangible heritage" for the city's heritage policy, noting it was previously removed. Members will research why it was removed and explore potential definitions.

chips.text: Recommended
Chair admitted not fully understanding intangible heritage, requesting more work.
The reason for removing intangible heritage from the policy remains unknown.
Committee members and staff will research past reports and definitions.

20.description: The committee recommends exploring partnerships with organizations like the WDM Heritage Festival to revitalize the Heritage Awards Program, given budget constraints.

chips.text: Recommended
Committee noted $17,000 budget is insufficient for a separate Heritage Awards dinner event.
Property owners who invest in heritage preservation could be recognized.
What are the costs associated with potential partnerships for the awards program?
Lenora suggested a partnership with the Design Council could be welcome.
A committee member will contact the WDM Heritage Festival organizers.

10.description: The committee recommends City Council receive information on expenditures totaling $17,082.

chips.text: Recommended
Taxpayers, for expenditures totaling $17,082.

12.description: The committee will attend a Planning, Development, & Community Services meeting on August 5, 2026, to discuss funding for a conference and ensure columns are repaired, not just painted.

chips.text: Recommended
Chairperson Southam noted a learning experience regarding report requirements for funding requests.
Attendees of a heritage convention may receive funding.
Chairperson Southam will attend the August 5th committee meeting.

16.description: A committee recommends receiving information on removing St. Mark's Anglican Church from a heritage holding bylaw, an atypical request as the property is for sale and redevelopment.

chips.text: Recommended
Staff noted the request to remove the designation without a demolition permit is unique.
The St. Mark's Anglican Church property at 1406 8th Avenue North is affected.
Administration will review the request and report back to Council.
